column11: two shares multiplied. (1) Genotype: 'nearly 90% of patients have at least one copy of the Phe508del mutation' (Middleton PG et al., N Engl J Med 2019;381:1809-1819, doi 10.1056/NEJMoa1908639), the variant the 1 to 2 year trial enrolled on, about 630 children a year. (2) One year of therapy each, 0.214225, the asset's discontinuation rate: a child started at 1 is outside the label for one year and inside it from the second birthday (label: 'aged 2 years and older', openFDA set f354423a-85c2-41c3-a9db-0f3aee135d8d). The engine keeps a layer's starts in a stock that decays at the asset's discontinuation rate, 1/0.214225 = 4.67 years of starts at steady state, so scaling the starts by 0.214225 leaves one patient-year a child, which is what the label leaves outside the base. 0.90 x 0.214225 = 0.192803
column12: the second factor is the age-out written into the pool, not a population share, and it holds only while discontinuation_pct is 0.214225: change one and change the other. It sits here rather than in base_pool_overlap_pct because the gate path (indication_layer.build, used by forecast_view._layer_gate) does not read the overlap, so an overlap of 0.786 would have priced the gate at 4.7 times the layer. On genotype it leans low, since the label also covers responsive non-F508del variants. On revenue it leans high: children homozygous for F508del can take Orkambi from age 1 and gating variants Kalydeco from 1 month, both Vertex products, so for them the layer is a switch inside Vertex rather than new revenue. No registry split by age was reachable to take them out
